story.head: Who blinks first?
paras: The Stars (10-6-2) lost 8-3 to Winnipeg on Thursday, and the Golden Knights (13-5-3) lost 3-2 in a shootout to Nashville on Friday. Going in, the Stars are fourth in the Central (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Knights second in the Pacific (fourth).

The Stars block more shots than anyone (1st) and have a dangerous power play (1st). As for the Golden Knights, they draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd). They also have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), and the Stars’ power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Stars (lowest), so expect a tight one.

Mikko Rantanen (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 18 GP) leads the Stars in scoring, with four goals in six games against Vegas since 2023-24. Jason Robertson (9 G / 11 A / 20 P in 18 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. For the Golden Knights, Jack Eichel (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, with six goals in nine games against Dallas since 2023-24. Mark Stone (10 G / 10 A / 20 P in 21 GP) has a team-high ten goals.

Jake Oettinger (9-4-1 / .895 SV% in 14 GS) will likely start for Dallas. Vegas has two options in net: Adin Hill (7-2-1 / .907 SV% in 10 GS) and Carter Hart (6-3-2 / .896 SV% in 11 GS). Hill has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
